definitions.explanation: A large, stately house and its grounds. Often associated with historical residences of samurai, nobles, or wealthy families. Also used for large modern houses.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{屋敷|やしき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}っている→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
⟦{武家|ぶけ}→武家：13242_buke⟧{屋敷|やしき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{観光地|かんこうち}→観光地：14163_kankouchi⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{公開|こうかい}→公開：11665_koukai⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A samurai residence is open to the public as a tourist attraction.
The vast estate built on the hill had both a garden and a storehouse.

notes:
USAGE:
{屋敷|やしき} evokes a sense of size and historical importance. It is commonly associated with the residences of ⟦{武士|ぶし}→武士：03989_bushi⟧ (samurai) and ⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧ (feudal lords) from the ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧. In modern usage, it can describe any impressively large house.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{邸宅|ていたく}→邸宅：14434_teitaku⟧: mansion, grand residence (more formal)
- ⟦{豪邸|ごうてい}→豪邸：18158_goutei⟧: magnificent mansion (emphasizes luxury)
- ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧: house (general, neutral)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{武家|ぶけ}→武家：13242_buke⟧{屋敷|やしき}: samurai residence
- ⟦{大名|だいみょう}→大名：10378_daimyou⟧{屋敷|やしき}: daimyo estate
- お{化|ば}け{屋敷|やしき}: haunted house
- {屋敷|やしき}{跡|あと}: site of a former mansion
